rv.q: a sumptuous musical about mental illness in suburbia

If not already obvious, every performer on stage gives a strong performance. With a cult following and complex subject matter, it's a difficult musical to bring to the stage, but they do it with grace and ease, aided by direction from Michael Longhurst. The cast is as strong vocally as they are with...
The cast's energy and talent is showcased and driven by an accomplished modern score, delivered by a 6-piece band who occupy 3 distinct panels above the main playing area.
The creative elements here are impossible to enthuse about: lightweight characters, flimsy music, forgettable costumes.
does not shy away from the harsh realities of mental illness and its impact on families.

The subject matter is of course not for everyone, and some are sure to be triggered, but with one in four of us experiencing some form of mental health problem every year, it is only right that such a production is afforded a platform of this scale.
